title: Rascal and Muffin's Leaf Sled Adventure
markdown:
Rascal the rabbit had ears that loved to dance and a nose that wiggled faster than a hundred jumping beans. His bestest, roundest pal was Muffin the guinea pig, fluffy as a soft cloud, eyes like tiny blueberries.

Rascal’s twitchy nose gave a super-duper wiggle. “Muffin. I have the most wonderful idea.”

Muffin was happily nibbling a juicy clover. She looked up, whiskers doing a little jig. “You always have the most wonderful ideas.”

Rascal puffed out his chest. “Today we deliver the prettiest daisy crown ever. For Mrs. Duck. She’ll quack with joy.”

Muffin’s whiskers wiggled like busy dancers. “A daisy crown. So kind. But how will we get there? The duck pond is quite a long hop.”

Rascal hopped from one foot to the other. “That’s the best part. We shall use a leaf sled.” He pointed at a giant green leaf near the stream, big enough for two little friends and a very important crown.

“A leaf sled.” Muffin giggled, tiny bells. “The most fun adventure.”

Hold tight, Muffin. We’re off.

Rascal’s idea was truly wonderful. He had already woven the crown behind the clover patch, every daisy bright and cheerful, smelling of sunshine and morning dew, and he had hidden it under a dock leaf so the bees would not borrow it. They placed it, oh-so-carefully, in the middle of the big green leaf, a pebble at each corner so it would not slide. Rascal gave a gentle nudge. The leaf floated into the shallow babbling stream. “Hop on.” Muffin hopped, round as a dumpling, and the leaf tipped, then settled.

The leaf sled drifted, bobbing. Rascal’s long floppy ears trailed in the breeze. He tried to steer with his front paws. Last week he had wanted a magnificent stick fort, and it had tumbled because he had tried it all by himself and gotten frustrated. “Hold tight, Muffin. We’re off. Grand delivery to the ducks.”

Steering was not as easy as he had imagined. The leaf spun. Rascal felt wobbly inside, the same wobble as the fallen fort. His ears drooped. “I’m not very good at steering. What if we go the wrong way. What if we end up in the puddles instead of the pond.”

Muffin, still and perfectly balanced, patted his paw. “It’s an adventure. Look how sparkly the water is. Liquid diamonds.” She pointed a tiny toe at sunbeams on the water.

A tiny shiny beetle with a shell like a polished button scuttled onto the bank and peered with beady eyes. “Hello. Having a bit of trouble with your leaf-boat?”

“Yes,” said Rascal, already a little better from Muffin’s words. “I’m trying to steer. It wobbles. I’m worried about getting lost.”

The beetle tapped a tiny foot. “Try a twig. A long sturdy twig can be a splendid rudder. It helps you push and pull the water.” He glanced at a tiny watch. “I must dash to my berry-meeting. I do hope this helps.”

“A twig,” Muffin squeaked. “Brilliant, Mr. Beetle. Thank you.”

Rascal’s eyes lit. He spotted a fallen twig, long and straight. With a hop and a wiggle he nudged it onto the leaf. He took a breath, remembered Muffin’s cheer, and dipped the twig. The leaf turned, smoother this time. “It works. Thank you, Mr. Beetle. You’re a genius.”

Hold tight, Muffin. We’re off.

A little further, the stream narrowed. Smooth round pebbles poked up like sleepy grey stones, and the current hurried as if it had remembered an appointment. Rascal gulped. The leaf nudged a pebble. Tap-tap-tap. The daisy crown wobbled toward the wet rim. His nose twitched. His tummy flipped. He nearly dropped the twig.

A friendly bright green face popped from the cool water. Ferdinand the Frog, eyes wide and round as emeralds. “Hello. Need a little help navigating this pebble patch? I was about to hop to that juicy fly, but I can help you first.”

“Ferdinand. This rocky bit. I don’t want to bump the crown.”

Ferdinand grinned a wide froggy grin. “Easy peasy.” A powerful flick of his long strong leg nudged the leaf past the pebbles. They glided as if on a smooth slide.

“You’re a lifesaver,” Muffin chirped, a little wiggle of thanks.

“Anytime,” Ferdinand called, a splash, then back into the cool water.

Soon a wonderful sound: the happy quacks of the duck family, first faint, then near. Reeds parted. The stream widened into the pond they had talked about all morning. On the grassy bank, Mrs. Duck and all her fluffy ducklings paddled in the sunshine, a trail of silver behind them.

“We’re here.” Rascal felt a flutter of pride. He had steered, with a little help, and they had made it. He guided the leaf right up to the edge, easy for Mrs. Duck to reach.

Mrs. Duck waddled over, eyes like dewdrops. “What a lovely surprise.”

Rascal hopped off, proud, and presented the crown. “For you. We made it all the way.”

Mrs. Duck beamed. She took the crown with her beak and set it carefully on her head. Perfectly splendid. The ducklings quacked and chirped, bobbing. “The prettiest crown we’ve ever seen,” one peeped, paddling.

Rascal felt warm from twitchy nose to fluffy tail. Muffin gave a happy squeak and a tiny nibble of stray clover. He remembered the wobble, and Muffin’s words, and Mr. Beetle’s twig, and Ferdinand’s flick. Hold tight, Muffin. We’re off. The sun shone on the pond, and on the crown, and on two friends who would take the long hop again — together, and with a rudder this time.
